entries.title: Combining resistance and aerobic training
entries.summary: Balance strength and aerobic goals while distinguishing added training from displaced endurance work.

entries.title: Deloads and fatigue management
entries.summary: Distinguish reduced-volume deloads, complete training breaks, and individual fatigue-management practice.

entries.title: Exercise selection, equipment and range of motion
entries.summary: Choose useful exercises and repeatable range of motion; distinguish equipment comparisons and deliberate lengthened partials.

entries.title: Training frequency and splits
entries.summary: Use frequency to distribute weekly work and fit a sustainable schedule.

entries.title: Load and repetition ranges
entries.summary: Choose loads for the desired strength skill, repeatable effort, and tolerable muscle work.

entries.title: Min-Max program context
entries.summary: Interpret original Phase 1 as a low-volume, high-effort program policy, with exact prescriptions kept in the authorized plan.

entries.title: The Muscle Ladder framework
entries.summary: Use a fundamentals-first coaching framework without treating book notes as a universal prescription.

entries.title: Progression and load adjustments
entries.summary: Use consistent technique, rep targets, and effort to make small, reviewable progression decisions.

entries.title: Proximity to failure and RIR
entries.summary: Use near-failure effort deliberately; distinguish estimated RIR, technical limits, and literal failure.

entries.title: Rest between working sets
entries.summary: Rest long enough to preserve set quality; exact timing is a practical choice with uncertain hypertrophy thresholds.

entries.title: Time-efficient training
entries.summary: Use reduced volume or sensible supersets to save time while watching effort and performance.

entries.title: Weekly volume for hypertrophy
entries.summary: Track challenging sets per muscle and adjust recoverable volume without treating a population average as a personal optimum.

entries.title: Assessment and readiness
entries.summary: Establish a useful baseline and respond proportionately to relevant symptoms, restrictions, and changes in readiness.

entries.title: Aerobic conditioning
entries.summary: Build aerobic activity from a tolerable baseline using understandable intensity and gradual progression.

entries.title: Adherence and recovery
entries.summary: Use feasible goals, a regular review, and recovery context without diagnosing causes from incomplete logs.

entries.title: Connect and identify the athlete
entries.summary: Connect with approve-on-phone sign-in, verify identity, discover operations and interpret CLI results.

entries.title: Establish and maintain individual context
entries.summary: Read and maintain the durable profile while separating unknowns and current session readiness.

entries.title: Author and revise a concrete program
entries.summary: Review saved coaching guides and complete authored frequency options; author, copy and schedule concrete prescriptions while preserving history.

entries.title: Coach and record a workout
entries.summary: Resume or start the right session, log actual work, manage timers and correct records.

entries.title: Review progress and adapt the individual plan
entries.summary: Review saved guide and actual training, adapt selected unstarted work in partial weeks and keep additional suggestions separate until selected.

entries.title: Interpret history, measurements, imports and exports
entries.summary: Import historical sessions through the API, use recorded body weight and outside workouts, and preserve status, identity, load and source semantics.

entries.title: Make deliberate, recoverable writes
entries.summary: Preserve editable fields and independent revisions and handle uncertainty and conflicts.

entries.title: Use evidence for an individual decision
entries.summary: Retrieve appropriate sources and separate findings, program conventions and coaching inference.

entries.title: Coach with Atlas
entries.summary: Use when an athlete asks for coaching, intake, programming, workout guidance, logging, history review, or training adjustments using Atlas.

entries.title: Design a training session
entries.summary: Use when designing or adapting one resistance-training workout, choosing exercise substitutions, or shortening a session for available equipment and time. Use training-program-design for multiweek structure.

entries.title: Build a program and choose a split
entries.summary: Use when building or comparing resistance-training programs, selecting a full-body, upper/lower or PPL split, or adapting a training block to goals and schedule. Excludes single-session edits and log-only progression decisions.

entries.title: Review training and progress
entries.summary: Use when reviewing workout logs, deciding whether to increase load, reps or volume, investigating a plateau, or adjusting effort and fatigue within a resistance-training program.

entries.title: Integrate conditioning and recovery
entries.summary: Use when integrating cardio or intervals with lifting, planning a hybrid-training week, or adjusting training demand for recovery. For mobility, stretching and yoga practice, use training-mobility-yoga.

entries.title: Mobility, stretching and yoga
entries.summary: Use when choosing mobility or flexibility work, static or dynamic stretching, pre-lift movement preparation, or yoga alongside training. Covers goal-specific dose, timing and reassessment; excludes diagnosis and individualized injury rehabilitation.

entries.title: Coaching context and evidence contract
entries.summary: Establish current facts, interpret records, and keep evidence, program convention and coaching inference separate before individualized advice.

entries.title: Session decisions
entries.summary: Substitutions, warm-up versus work sets, short-session trade-offs and effort endpoints for one workout.

entries.title: Stimulus and fatigue: choose exercises by what they cost
entries.summary: Stimulus-to-fatigue ratio: each exercise's fatigue rating and limiting factor, the session stacking score and caps, Effort by exercise type, fatigue signals, and options for reducing demand.

entries.title: Split decisions
entries.summary: Choose full-body, upper/lower, PPL or rolling splits by the schedule that actually happens; allocate and audit weekly work.

entries.title: Program modes
entries.summary: Hypertrophy-first, strength, time-constrained or maintenance, minimal-equipment and named-program modes for program design.

entries.title: Progression decisions
entries.summary: Reconcile records before calculating, then choose progress, repeat, adjust, investigate a plateau or change volume.

entries.title: Hybrid and recovery decisions
entries.summary: Place and dose conditioning around the chosen priority and review recoverability without over-reading fatigue.

entries.title: Is routine failure needed in multi-set training?
entries.summary: Dated source check: repeated true failure is not established as a blanket requirement; exact individual effort targets remain uncertain.

entries.title: Shorter sessions without sacrificing recovery
entries.summary: Dated source check: antagonist supersets and rest timing can save time; exact equivalence and fixed rest ceilings are not established.

entries.title: Source checks for the coaching skills
entries.summary: Dated source checks behind the coaching skills: weekly volume and frequency, autoregulation, concurrent training and the HIIT duration model.

entries.title: How heavy warm-up sets should be
entries.summary: Dated source check: one warm-up set near the working load prepares better than light sets alone; exact ramp percentages are convention.

entries.title: Mobility, stretching and yoga: evidence check
entries.summary: Dated source check: separate movement preparation, longer-term range of motion and optional yoga or relaxation; stretching dose and timing evidence.

entries.title: Open research questions
entries.summary: A research queue of unresolved coaching questions, with what would resolve each; not a prescribed program.

entries.title: Concurrent training interference
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-03), not re-checked: Concurrent endurance and resistance training was reported to preserve whole-muscle growth and maximal strength on average.

entries.title: Long muscle length training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-04), not re-checked: The imported reviews favor considering tension at longer muscle lengths, while leaving superiority of lengthened partials over full-range repetitions unsettled.

entries.title: VO2max HIIT protocols
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-05), not re-checked: The cited syntheses report aerobic-fitness improvements from both intervals and continuous exercise, with intervals potentially offering time savings.

entries.title: Beginner calisthenics integration
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-06), not re-checked: A short push-up progression trial and an older progression position stand support treating bodyweight exercise as progressively dosed resistance work.

entries.title: Inter-set rest hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-07), not re-checked: The imported rest review suggests a small growth advantage above very short rest intervals, with uncertain differences among longer rests.

entries.title: Deloads fatigue management
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-08), not re-checked: A deload consensus statement and a trial of one week without training address different interventions.

entries.title: Exercise order prioritization
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-09), not re-checked: The cited syntheses associate earlier exercise placement with greater strength improvement in that exercise.

entries.title: Training frequency hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-10), not re-checked: Volume-equated frequency comparisons suggest frequency alone has a limited effect on muscle growth.

entries.title: Zone 2 HIIT hybrid conditioning
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-11), not re-checked: Low-intensity endurance exercise and interval training were both reported to improve aerobic fitness.

entries.title: Tendon load management
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-12), not re-checked: Reviews in tendinopathy populations support progressive resistance loading, but do not identify a single best protocol across tendon conditions.

entries.title: Loaded carries hybrid accessory
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-13), not re-checked: Carry research includes biomechanics, muscle-activation studies, and load-carriage performance research.

entries.title: Proximity to failure RIR
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-14), not re-checked: The imported failure literature distinguishes working near failure from reaching momentary failure on every set.

entries.title: Free weights machines hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-15), not re-checked: Direct comparisons report broadly similar muscle-growth outcomes for machines and free weights.

entries.title: Supersets time efficient hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-16), not re-checked: Superset studies suggest shorter sessions with broadly comparable chronic outcomes in a small evidence base.

entries.title: Range of motion hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-17), not re-checked: The cited range-of-motion literature favors distinguishing full range, long-length partials, and short-length partials.

entries.title: Deloads periodization fatigue
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-18), not re-checked: Volume-matched periodization research reports clearer support for strength than for additional muscle growth.

entries.title: Warmups ramp sets
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-19), not re-checked: Warm-up reviews address acute readiness and performance rather than demonstrating additional muscle growth.

entries.title: Weekly volume hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-20), not re-checked: The imported volume syntheses associate more weekly sets with greater average growth, subject to diminishing returns.

entries.title: Concurrent training sequencing
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-21), not re-checked: Sequencing research separates whole-muscle growth, maximal strength, and explosive performance.

entries.title: Repetition tempo hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-22), not re-checked: The cited tempo reviews report little clear growth difference across commonly studied repetition speeds.

entries.title: Exercise selection variation
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-23), not re-checked: Planned exercise variation and single- versus multi-joint comparisons address different questions.

entries.title: Resistance training prescription hierarchy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-24), not re-checked: The imported overviews emphasize resistance training itself, training volume, and goal-specific prescription rather than universal superiority of advanced methods.

entries.title: Plyometrics hybrid training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-25), not re-checked: Plyometric research primarily supports examining jumping, sprinting, and power outcomes.

entries.title: Blood flow restriction training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-05-26), not re-checked: Blood-flow-restriction studies examine whether low-load exercise can become more effective with occlusion.

entries.title: Unilateral vs. bilateral training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-01), not re-checked: The imported unilateral/bilateral synthesis reports no clear average growth difference in a limited literature.

entries.title: Grip strength training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-02), not re-checked: Grip strength can be a health marker without proving that isolated grip training changes long-term health outcomes.

entries.title: Eccentric tempo
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-03), not re-checked: The eccentric-duration review has a small evidence base and uncertain hypertrophy estimates.

entries.title: Unstable surface training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-04), not re-checked: Unstable-surface exercise may improve balance, but its superiority to stable-surface resistance training depends on the task and population.

entries.title: Velocity loss thresholds
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-05), not re-checked: Higher velocity loss usually entails more repetitions and acute fatigue, so comparisons can confound fatigue threshold with accumulated work.

entries.title: Exercise snacks
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-06), not re-checked: Exercise-snack reviews report improved aerobic fitness, particularly in physically inactive adults.

entries.title: Advanced training methods
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-07), not re-checked: The imported advanced-method reviews do not show a clear aggregate hypertrophy advantage over traditional sets.

entries.title: Minimal dose resistance training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-08), not re-checked: The cited network meta-analysis reports benefits from many resistance-training prescriptions compared with no exercise.

entries.title: Weekly hypertrophy focus periodization
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-09), not re-checked: Volume-matched comparisons do not establish a special hypertrophy benefit from periodization itself.

entries.title: Autoregulated load progression
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-10), not re-checked: Autoregulated and percentage-based loading produced similar overall strength results in one cited synthesis, while a later network analysis ranked some autoregulated approaches more favorably.

entries.title: ACSM resistance training position stand
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-11), not re-checked: The imported ACSM overview describes broad benefits from progressive resistance training and goal-specific refinements.

entries.title: Cluster sets and advanced methods
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-12), not re-checked: Cluster-set evidence suggests broadly comparable chronic adaptations with possible reductions in within-session fatigue.

entries.title: Low volume HIIT
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-13), not re-checked: The low-volume interval review reports fitness improvements in non-athlete adults with brief sessions.

entries.title: Zone 2 intensity prescription
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-14), not re-checked: The imported expert viewpoint defines a low-intensity zone using physiological thresholds rather than a universal heart-rate percentage.

entries.title: Sleep deprivation training performance
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-15), not re-checked: The imported sleep-loss synthesis reports impaired performance across several domains and higher perceived effort.

entries.title: Scapular control calisthenics prep
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-16), not re-checked: Shoulder-therapy trials and scapular muscle-activation studies concern different populations and outcomes.

entries.title: Drop sets time efficient hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-17), not re-checked: Small drop-set syntheses report similar average growth to conventional sets with time savings in some protocols.

entries.title: Rest-pause advanced methods
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-18), not re-checked: The cited advanced-method review reports a possible rest-pause growth signal within otherwise uncertain aggregate hypertrophy comparisons.

entries.title: Static stretching hypertrophy ROM
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-19), not re-checked: Static-stretching reviews report reliable flexibility effects and smaller, less certain muscle-size effects, often under unusually large stretching doses.

entries.title: Exercise order prioritization
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-20), not re-checked: The exercise-order meta-analysis reports greater strength gains in movements trained earlier.

entries.title: Sprint interval training BP VO2
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-21), not re-checked: A small cycling-based sprint-interval comparison reports improvements in aerobic fitness and some blood-pressure outcomes with both interval and continuous training.

entries.title: Bracing valsalva resistance training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-22), not re-checked: The cited reviews describe pressure and trunk-stability effects of bracing and breath holding.

entries.title: Cold water immersion hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-23), not re-checked: The imported cold-water syntheses suggest that repeated immersion soon after lifting may attenuate growth or strength adaptation.

entries.title: Heat resistance training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-24), not re-checked: The heat review combines plausible mechanisms with limited direct training evidence.

entries.title: Concurrent training modality
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-25), not re-checked: Concurrent-training modality comparisons are limited by small datasets and heterogeneity.

entries.title: Lifting straps grip limited pulling
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-26), not re-checked: The straps literature described here is mainly exploratory or acute.

entries.title: Myo-reps time efficient hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-27), not re-checked: The imported short myo-reps trial reports similar measured adaptations in less training time.

entries.title: Attentional focus mind-muscle
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-28), not re-checked: Attentional-focus studies suggest that external cues can aid immediate force output, while direct growth evidence is sparse and muscle-specific.

entries.title: Foam rolling warmup recovery
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-29), not re-checked: Foam-rolling research describes possible short-term mobility or perceived-recovery benefits without a clear special performance advantage over other warm-ups.

entries.title: Wrist loading calisthenics prep
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-06-30), not re-checked: The cited wrist-loading evidence comes largely from young gymnasts and overuse-injury literature.

entries.title: Technique hypertrophy priorities
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-01), not re-checked: A narrative technique review discusses controlled movement, range, and exercise-specific flexibility, while a separate synthesis addresses broader training prescriptions.

entries.title: Feedback supervision resistance training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-02), not re-checked: Feedback and supervision studies report acute performance and some longer-term strength benefits.

entries.title: Inter-set static stretching
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-03), not re-checked: Inter-set stretching has mechanistic appeal but limited comparative evidence.

entries.title: Flywheel resistance training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-04), not re-checked: Flywheel reviews support investigation of eccentric-loading and power outcomes, with uncertain superiority for maximal strength or hypertrophy.

entries.title: Single vs. multiple sets
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-05), not re-checked: The imported syntheses favor multiple sets on average for hypertrophy while also reporting benefits from lower-dose prescriptions.

entries.title: Exercise selection variation
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-06), not re-checked: Exercise-selection reviews distinguish regional targeting, whole-muscle growth, and movement-specific strength.

entries.title: Resistance training prescription variables
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-07), not re-checked: The cited network meta-analysis compares combinations of loading, set number, and frequency.

entries.title: Repetition tempo hypertrophy update
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-08), not re-checked: The newer tempo synthesis reports a small, imprecise direct difference between faster and slower repetitions.

entries.title: Proximity to failure dose response update
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-09), not re-checked: The updated failure note distinguishes estimated-proximity associations from direct failure-versus-nonfailure comparisons.

entries.title: ROM long-length partials update
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-10), not re-checked: The imported range reviews favor examining the muscle lengths trained and the strength range tested.

entries.title: Velocity loss thresholds performance
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-11), not re-checked: Lower velocity-loss thresholds were associated with better velocity or sprint outcomes in the cited lower-body reviews.

entries.title: Resistance training blood pressure
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-12), not re-checked: The imported blood-pressure reviews report average reductions from regular resistance training, mainly in hypertensive or clinical populations.

entries.title: Isometric resistance training blood pressure
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-13), not re-checked: The cited isometric-training synthesis reports lower office blood pressure in adults with hypertension, with less consistent ambulatory results.

entries.title: Advanced training methods hypertrophy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-14), not re-checked: The advanced-method update again reports uncertain aggregate hypertrophy superiority despite more favorable strength findings.

entries.title: Resistance training prescription hierarchy
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-15), not re-checked: The imported prescription reviews place stronger emphasis on training participation, sets, and goal-specific loading than on fine adjustments.

entries.title: Cooling strategies resistance training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-16), not re-checked: The palm/sole-cooling synthesis was a preprint and reported uncertain acute performance effects.

entries.title: Carbohydrate fueling resistance training
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-17), not re-checked: The imported nutrition literature suggests carbohydrate effects on lifting performance depend on prior feeding, depletion, and training volume.

entries.title: Rotator cuff shoulder prep
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-18), not re-checked: Shoulder-therapy reviews suggest some value in tailored progressive exercise, but uncertainty remains about the best formula.

entries.title: Progressive push-up calisthenics
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-07-19), not re-checked: Small, short push-up studies suggest that adequately progressed bodyweight pressing can produce strength and, in some trials, muscle-size gains.

entries.title: ACSM resistance training position stand
entries.summary: Older research pointer (2026-09-12), not re-checked: The later ACSM note describes the same broad position-stand framework as earlier entries, with an additional plain-language locator.

entries.title: Reduced dose maintenance training

entries.title: mHealth resistance training evidence

entries.title: Early consistency long-term adherence

entries.title: Resistance training adherence interventions
